newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shrs end up, secondary stocks offer bargains.
newsitem.headline: Lima shrs end up, secondary stocks offer bargains.

text.p: The Lima stock exchange continued last week's upward trend by rising Monday as investors found bargains in second- and third-tier stocks, brokers said.
They added prices were expected to climb again Tuesday.
Monday, the General Index rose 1.96 percent to 1,531.1 points, while the blue-chip Selective Index climbed 0.83 percent to 2,082.8 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
In a total of 2,636 trades, 61 stocks rose, 16 fell and 30 were stable, where volume fell to a modest 28.3 million ($11.4 million) down from 43.6 million soles on Friday.

The lower volume allowed trade in normally less important companies to have more effect on the market's overall movement. These stocks offered bargains Monday because last week they lagged behind the rises in leaders, brokers said.
"The lower tiers saw strong trade," said Arlen Lahura of the local brokerage Interlima. "They were way behind (last week's) movements."
Among leaders, benchmark Telefnica del Per bucked the upward trend by slipping 0.18 percent to 5.68 soles in low volume accounting for 11 percent of the day's total trade.

Buenaventura rose 0.23 percent to 21.55 soles as the stock continued to climb on last week's news that the polymetal miner had won a lawsuit to exercise preemptive rights on shares in Peru's largest gold project Yanacocha.
Buenaventura accounted for seven percent of the day's trade.
Brewery Backus y Johnston rose 1.10 percent to 2.70 soles, accounting for 11 percent of total volume.
